brief: Owner, 2026-11-26: Fable 5.2 usage in the Claude allowance is too high. Keep Fable for the state-of-the-art check, but make that check less frequent and use cheaper models for the work.
tradeoff: Fewer Fable calls can miss a product trade-off until the next phase gate, and a batched decision can be less tailored than a per-task one. In return, the expensive model reviews direction and true trade-offs rather than routine confirmations.
entry: Fable is called at most once per phase, and only for a new product trade-off, a direction review, or a decision not derivable from a recorded decision. All pending questions are batched into that call. Routine priority confirmations, single decisions covered by a decision id, and per-task checks do not use Fable. The advisor has the same budget: one call per task after two failed attempts on the same question. Opus 5.5 remains the per-task Refine and Check model; Sonnet 5.5 carries architecture, adversarial and UX review; Build/Fix, QA and helpers use zero-cost OpenCode Go models. Escalation to Fable happens only when those disagree or a product trade-off remains. If a Fable call would only confirm existing policy, the lead cites the decision and does not call.
serves: Owner, 2026-11-26; the Claude allowance; PRODUCT.md quality bar.
